summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Apple’s installment payments target affordability
articles.description: Amid price increases, the iPhone maker’s CEO says a new lease program run by BNPL player Klarna is designed to boost consumers’ ability to buy.

articles.title: Why fintechs may skirt the US
articles.description: “There are clear signs that leading payments players and fintechs may be pulling out of the U.S. to prioritize other, more ‘open banking-friendly’ regions,” writes one financial software executive.

articles.title: Capital One provides Discover community investment update
articles.description: The bank issued a report last month on progress related to the $265 billion it had committed to invest as part of its bid to buy Discover Financial Services. Charitable organizations working with it offered little support for the statement.

articles.title: Stablecoins complement dollar: Fed
articles.description: The greenback will retain its dominance as stablecoins increasingly shape cross-border payments, speakers at a Fed conference predicted.

articles.title: Visa’s revenue momentum slows
articles.description: The card network’s recent revenue growth slowed in July, relative to last year, but customer spending remains healthy, the company said.

articles.title: Pex aims to expand card biz
articles.description: The spend-management firm raised money from investors to grow its corporate card and finance software business.

articles.title: PayPal leans into financial services
articles.description: The company’s CEO said that buy now, pay later and other consumer finance offerings will pump up revenue, but some analysts have doubts.

articles.title: How ISO consolidation persists
articles.description: Global Payments and other processors have been gobbling up smaller firms for years, but payments professionals keep forming new ones.
